notes: The Delhi Metro is clean, cheap and air-conditioned, with a women's carriage. Uber and Ola are safe; bargain with auto-rickshaw drivers. Take the Gatimaan Express to Agra and the Shatabdi to Jaipur.

From June to September it is 38-45°C with monsoon rain: sightsee from 08:00 to 11:00 and after 16:00, spend midday somewhere air-conditioned, drink 3-4 litres of water a day and see the Taj at sunrise.
Monument entry costs foreign visitors 500-600 INR (35 for Indians); an online ASI ticket skips the queue. The Taj is closed on Fridays and the Red Fort on Mondays.
Choose street food that is freshly cooked and hot, and skip ice and raw salad. Stick to bottled water and bring probiotics against Delhi belly.
Take your shoes off at temples and mosques and cover shoulders and knees. Keep your head covered in Sikh gurdwaras, where food is free.
Tip 10%. Bargaining applies everywhere: start at a third of the first price.

stops.name: Jama Masjid
stops.tips: India's largest mosque. Climb the minaret for the view (separate ticket); cover shoulders and knees, and leave your shoes outside.

stops.name: Chandni Chowk
stops.tips: Old Delhi's main bazaar. Take a rickshaw through the narrow lanes and visit the Khari Baoli spice market.

stops.name: Paranthe Wali Gali
stops.tips: A lane of stuffed paratha fried in ghee, open since the 1870s, with 3-4 varieties to choose from.

stops.name: Red Fort
stops.tips: Shah Jahan's red fortress and a UNESCO site. Foreign visitors pay 600 INR; closed on Mondays.

stops.name: Karim's Jama Masjid
stops.tips: Mughal cooking since 1913, on the lane facing the mosque. Order the mutton burra and nihari.

backups.name: Al Jawahar Restaurant
backups.tips: Karim's rival across the road, for kebabs and korma.

backups.name: Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib
backups.tips: A Sikh temple on Chandni Chowk with free langar (communal meal). Keep your head covered.

stops.name: Humayun's Tomb
stops.tips: The Mughal tomb that preceded the Taj Mahal. Come for the morning light and the gardens.

stops.name: Nizamuddin Dargah
stops.tips: A Sufi shrine with qawwali music on Thursday evenings, set in narrow lanes.

stops.name: Lodhi Garden
stops.tips: A park among 15th-century tombs and the calmest spot in Delhi.

stops.name: Khan Market
stops.tips: A stylish market with kathi rolls at Khan Chacha and plenty of bookshops.

stops.name: India Gate
stops.tips: A war memorial on Rajpath. In the evening it fills with families and ice cream.

backups.name: Sodabottleopenerwala Khan Market
backups.tips: A Parsi café; try the berry pulao.

backups.name: National Museum Delhi
backups.tips: Harappan finds and Mughal miniatures, an indoor option when it is hot.

stops.name: Qutub Minar
stops.tips: A 73 m minaret from the 12th century, with a rust-free iron pillar. Mornings are cooler.

stops.name: Mehrauli Archaeological Park
stops.tips: A free park of ruins next to the Qutub complex, including Jamali Kamali.

stops.name: Hauz Khas Village
stops.tips: Lakeside madrasa ruins, boutiques and cafés.

stops.name: Hauz Khas Social
stops.tips: A café-bar with lake views, good for lunch.

stops.name: Lotus Temple
stops.tips: A Bahai house of worship shaped like a lotus. Quiet inside; closed on Mondays.

backups.name: Dilli Haat INA
backups.tips: A crafts market with regional food stalls, an alternative to the temple.

stops.name: Taj Mahal
stops.tips: Take the 08:10 Gatimaan Express (1.5 hours) or leave by car at 05:00. Buy a sunrise ticket (1,100 plus 200 for the mausoleum); closed on Fridays. Shoe covers are provided.

stops.name: Agra Fort
stops.tips: The fort where Shah Jahan was imprisoned. You can see the Taj across the river.

stops.name: Pinch of Spice Agra
stops.tips: North Indian cooking in Agra, air-conditioned.

stops.name: Itmad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj)
stops.tips: A small tomb that pioneered marble inlay work, without the crowds.

stops.name: Mehtab Bagh
stops.tips: A garden across the river, green in the monsoon months.

backups.name: Joney's Place Agra
backups.tips: A backpacker classic; order a lassi.

backups.name: Fatehpur Sikri
backups.tips: The abandoned Mughal capital (40 km away), an alternative to Baby Taj.

stops.name: Amber Fort
stops.tips: It is 4-5 hours from Delhi by train or car, so ideally stay a night. The hilltop mirror palace is reached by jeep rather than elephant.

stops.name: Hawa Mahal
stops.tips: The Palace of Winds facade. Take your photo from the café opposite.

stops.name: City Palace Jaipur
stops.tips: The Maharaja's palace and museum, at the heart of the Pink City.

stops.name: Laxmi Misthan Bhandar
stops.tips: A sweet shop and restaurant since 1727. Try the dal bati and ghewar.

stops.name: Johari Bazaar
stops.tips: A market for jewellery and block-printed fabric. Bargain.

backups.name: Jantar Mantar Jaipur
backups.tips: Giant stone astronomical instruments, an alternative to the palace.

backups.name: Rawat Misthan Bhandar
backups.tips: Pyaz kachori (onion-stuffed pastry), Jaipur's street food favourite.

stops.name: Akshardham Temple
stops.tips: A vast, modern Hindu temple complex. Phones and cameras are not allowed (leave them in the cloakroom); the exhibitions cost about 250 INR.

stops.name: Connaught Place
stops.tips: A circular market with white colonnades, at the centre of Delhi.

stops.name: Saravana Bhavan Connaught Place
stops.tips: South Indian thali and dosa, air-conditioned.

stops.name: Janpath Market
stops.tips: Tibetan market stalls and textiles. Bargain.

stops.name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
stops.tips: A golden-domed Sikh temple with a sacred pool and a langar kitchen.

backups.name: Agrasen ki Baoli
backups.tips: A stepwell near Janpath, good for photos.

days.theme: Morning market and a gentle farewell

stops.name: Sunder Nursery
stops.tips: A restored Mughal garden beside Humayun's Tomb. Take a morning walk; on Sundays there is an organic market.

stops.name: Cafe Lota Pragati Maidan
stops.tips: Modern Indian breakfast and lunch in the garden of the crafts museum, for a farewell meal.

stops.name: National Crafts Museum
stops.tips: A crafts museum with master artisans at work, good for souvenirs.

stops.name: Delhi Metro Airport Express
stops.tips: It takes 20 minutes from New Delhi station to the airport, a quick goodbye.

backups.name: Andhra Bhavan Canteen
backups.tips: A cheap, unlimited thali and a Delhi legend.

backups.name: Purana Qila
backups.tips: The Old Fort and its lake, an alternative to the museum.
